Definition: something saved, i.e. (abstractly) deliverance; hence, aid, victory, prosperity
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, yᵉshûwʻâh means salvation, deliverance. In Genesis 49:18, I have waited for thy salvation. Across its 76 occurrences, the word keeps that same sense, whether the setting is promise or warning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe salvation is not a word for the end of the story only; it is God's rescue breaking into the present, and I have seen Him save in the middle of trouble, not only after it. That is why I come back to yᵉshûwʻâh whenever I need to remember what is true.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
